variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: An autonomous system repeatedly senses an environment, estimates what is happening, chooses a plan, and controls a physical or digital process with limited moment-to-moment human direction. A warehouse robot, inspection drone, and automated vehicle have different mechanics, but they share one defining property: their actions change the environment that produces the next observation.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Observe the environment
pairs.detail: Collect timestamped measurements and health signals from cameras, lidar, radar, inertial units, encoders, maps, application events, or other domain sensors.
pairs.explanation: Collect timestamped measurements and health signals from cameras, lidar, radar, inertial units, encoders, maps, application events, or other domain sensors.

pairs.label: Infer a belief state
pairs.detail: Fuse current and prior evidence into position, motion, objects, free space, intent, and uncertainty rather than treating one model output as ground truth.
pairs.explanation: Fuse current and prior evidence into position, motion, objects, free space, intent, and uncertainty rather than treating one model output as ground truth.

pairs.label: Select a bounded action
pairs.detail: Generate feasible trajectories or decisions, reject candidates that violate constraints, and expose the assumptions behind the chosen plan.
pairs.explanation: Generate feasible trajectories or decisions, reject candidates that violate constraints, and expose the assumptions behind the chosen plan.

pairs.label: Act, measure, and correct
pairs.detail: Track the bounded command, compare expected and measured response, revoke authority when limits fail, and begin the next loop from fresh evidence.
pairs.explanation: Track the bounded command, compare expected and measured response, revoke authority when limits fail, and begin the next loop from fresh evidence.

pairs.label: Operating domain
pairs.detail: Name environmental ranges, map coverage, lighting, weather, traffic, surface conditions, payload, speed, communication, and supervision assumptions.
pairs.explanation: Name environmental ranges, map coverage, lighting, weather, traffic, surface conditions, payload, speed, communication, and supervision assumptions.

pairs.label: Authority boundary
pairs.detail: Limit speed, acceleration, force, route, resource use, and control duration.
pairs.explanation: Limit speed, acceleration, force, route, resource use, and control duration. A planner proposes; a separate gate decides whether the command is allowed.

pairs.label: Safe state
pairs.detail: Define a state the system can actually reach after a fault: hold position, controlled landing, limited motion, service isolation, or human handoff.
pairs.explanation: Define a state the system can actually reach after a fault: hold position, controlled landing, limited motion, service isolation, or human handoff.

pairs.label: Evidence contract
pairs.detail: Connect each safety and performance claim to scenario coverage, fault injection, hardware timing, replay, field monitoring, and an accountable owner.
pairs.explanation: Connect each safety and performance claim to scenario coverage, fault injection, hardware timing, replay, field monitoring, and an accountable owner.

pairs.label: Detection and classification
pairs.detail: Identify objects, free space, landmarks, anomalies, or events.
pairs.explanation: Identify objects, free space, landmarks, anomalies, or events. Report calibrated scores, timestamps, sensor origin, and the conditions under which the detector was evaluated.

pairs.label: Tracking and motion
pairs.detail: Associate observations across time and estimate velocity, acceleration, intent, and uncertainty.
pairs.explanation: Associate observations across time and estimate velocity, acceleration, intent, and uncertainty. A track must survive short occlusion without inventing certainty.

pairs.label: Localization and mapping
pairs.detail: Estimate pose relative to a map or local frame.
pairs.explanation: Estimate pose relative to a map or local frame. Carry covariance and map validity so planning can widen margins or stop when pose becomes ambiguous.

pairs.label: Sensor fusion
pairs.detail: Align time and coordinates before combining modalities.
pairs.explanation: Align time and coordinates before combining modalities. Preserve disagreement as a fault signal; averaging incompatible evidence can hide the exact condition that requires fallback.

pairs.label: Test components against contracts
pairs.detail: Check perception calibration, state update invariants, planner feasibility, command limits, and monitor logic with deterministic fixtures and protected incident traces.
pairs.explanation: Check perception calibration, state update invariants, planner feasibility, command limits, and monitor logic with deterministic fixtures and protected incident traces.

pairs.label: Explore scenario boundaries
pairs.detail: Vary geometry, agents, weather, lighting, sensor noise, timing, maps, and policy while measuring both expected behavior and fallback transitions.
pairs.explanation: Vary geometry, agents, weather, lighting, sensor noise, timing, maps, and policy while measuring both expected behavior and fallback transitions.

pairs.label: Preserve physical timing
pairs.detail: Run production compute, buses, sensors, controllers, and actuators so queueing, synchronization, saturation, and transfer latency remain visible.
pairs.explanation: Run production compute, buses, sensors, controllers, and actuators so queueing, synchronization, saturation, and transfer latency remain visible.

pairs.label: Expand the domain gradually
pairs.detail: Start inside a narrow envelope, compare field traces with predictions, maintain rollback and stop authority, and widen only when evidence supports the new claim.
pairs.explanation: Start inside a narrow envelope, compare field traces with predictions, maintain rollback and stop authority, and widen only when evidence supports the new claim.

It must use a camera
It cannot contain deterministic software
It always operates without a human supervisor
variants.explanation: Autonomy closes a feedback loop: sensing changes decisions, actions change the environment, and the changed environment produces the next evidence.

variants.prompt: A robot travels at 4 m/s, has a 0.25 s reaction delay, and can decelerate at 4 m/s^2. What is its idealized stopping distance before adding clearance and uncertainty?
options: 1 m
2 m
3 m
5 m
variants.explanation: Reaction distance is 4 x 0.25 = 1 m. Braking distance is v^2/(2a) = 16/8 = 2 m, so the total is 3 m before safety reserves.

variants.prompt: What is the main value of an independent runtime assurance monitor?

It can revoke primary authority using a simpler, separately justified safety path
It removes the need for fault injection

variants.explanation: A monitor that is sufficiently independent can catch timing, health, uncertainty, or command-boundary violations even when the primary autonomy stack is wrong.

variants.prompt: Why is nominal simulation alone weak release evidence?
options: Simulation cannot produce sensor data
It does not establish behavior across targeted edge cases, injected faults, hardware timing, and recovery paths
Only public-road testing can measure latency
Nominal scenarios are always harder than rare scenarios
variants.explanation: A safety claim needs evidence across the operating domain and known failure modes, including closed-loop timing and fallback behavior, not only average nominal performance.
